Job Description
Kickstart Your Career at Vertex! 
Are you ready to make a real impact? At Vertex, our mission is to tackle serious diseases and to change lives, for the better, for the future. Our aim is to give you the skills, insights, and career guidance to be an important part of that future; to turn your potential into progression. As a Vertex intern or co-op, you’ll work on meaningful projects, collaborate with talented teams, and learn from industry leaders. We’re passionate about innovation, inclusion, and supporting your growth—inside and outside the lab. 
Why Vertex?

Your Impact
The Vertex Process Chemistry Co-Op is a 6-month experiential training program for students currently working towards a bachelor's or master's degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biochemistry or other related fields. If you are passionate, collaborative, and growth-minded, a co-op at Vertex will help you gain meaningful experience in our Process Chemistry functional areas and serve as a launchpad for your career.
The application deadline for this co-op is November 15th. Please note that Vertex reviews applications on a rolling basis and reserves the right to close this job posting prior to the listed deadline. Applicants can expect to receive an update about their application before or shortly after the application deadline.
Ready to apply? Submit your application and let’s turn possibilities into reality! 
 What you will be doing: 
Vertex Process Chemistry is seeking a highly motivated and scientifically curious co-op student to join our team in January of 2027. Within Process Chemistry, scientists apply their expertise in organic synthetic chemistry to develop and execute scalable manufacturing processes of active pharmaceutical ingredients as these novel therapeutics undergo clinical trials.
This role offers the opportunity to directly contribute to impactful process development research at Vertex while working with Process Chemistry and Engineering scientists in our collaborative, fast-paced environment. With thorough training and hands-on experience, the co-op will support the application of advanced technologies for the optimization and scale-up of photoredox catalysis, including high-throughput experimentation, flow chemistry, and machine learning tools.
Key Responsibilities:
As a Process Chemistry Co-op, you will have the opportunity to:
Train in advanced laboratory & experimental design techniques (flow chemistry, photochemistry, Design-of-Experiments [DoE], Bayesian optimization, etc.).
Work closely with a team of chemists and engineers to design novel chemical experiments through group discussion and collaboration.
Apply good laboratory techniques to the syntheses of complex organic compounds according to the developed research plan.
Maintain a thorough record of your work through a detailed and clearly written electronic laboratory notebook.
Evaluate reaction optimization techniques for photoredox catalysis.
Develop a substrate scope, determine functional group tolerance, identify reactivity limitations, and evaluate reaction kinetics under the conditions identified in reaction optimization.
Use scientific literature to guide experimental design and interpret results.
Present project progress and experimental data, and recommendations to the project team.
Once trained, operate and interpret data from relevant analytical instruments (e.g. NMR, HPLC, GC, LC-MS, IR, etc.).
Deliver a presentation to the Process Chemistry department and prepare a research summary document upon the completion of the co-op.

Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degrees in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a closely related field.
Third-year undergraduate student or above at the start of the co-op term.
Completion of undergraduate organic chemistry coursework and associated laboratory courses.
Strong interest in synthetic organic chemistry, catalysis, process chemistry, or pharmaceutical development.
Ability to work safely, independently, and collaboratively in a laboratory environment.
Strong organization, documentation, problem-solving, and both written and verbal communication skills.
Legal authorization to work in the United States, now and in the future. Please note that Vertex does not provide sponsorship for internships/co-ops or entry level roles within this part of the organization.

Previous internship, undergraduate research, or laboratory experience.
Prior experience in synthetic organic chemistry research is preferred but not required.
Familiarity with one or more analytical techniques (e.g. NMR, HPLC, GC, LC-MS, IR, etc.).
Experience searching scientific literature, patents, and chemical databases.
Demonstrated ability to analyze and organize experimental results and communicate scientific findings clearly.

About the Team/Role:
We are seeking an inquisitive, proactive, and analytical Software Engineering Intern to join our Enterprise Applications & Systems Engineering organization. In this role, you will participate in solving a critical enterprise challenge: establishing a customer repository within our core enterprise architecture and CRM (Salesforce) by unifying data funneled through our modern data warehouse (Snowflake).
As our business scales across diverse commercial platforms, customer and account data originates across multiple legacy systems, transactional processing engines, and operational datastores. You will act as both a technical detective and a systems builder—collaborating with senior enterprise architects, software engineers, and business leaders to sleuth out golden record sources, gather requirements for essential customer attributes, and design reusable data ingestion and transformation patterns.
This internship offers hands-on enterprise systems experience, active mentorship from senior engineering leaders, and direct exposure to modern cloud data stacks and CRM architectures.
How you’ll make an impact:
Investigate Source Systems: Trace data lineage across disparate systems (billing platforms, transactional processors, legacy portals, and operational services) to identify where key customer, account, and relationship attributes truly originate.
Define Customer Schema: Partner with product managers, business analysts, and functional leads across Sales, Service, and Operations to document requirements for what constitutes the "single source of truth" for customer identity in Salesforce.
Data Quality & Validation: Perform exploratory data analysis to evaluate consistency, detect schema drift, address duplicate records, and define mapping rules between upstream source models and their desitnations.
Build for Reusability: Assist in designing and building scalable, modular data extraction, transformation, and ingestion workflows so future source integrations can plug in with minimal custom code.
Harness Snowflake: Write optimized SQL transformations, views, and data processing routines within Snowflake to clean, normalize, and stage customer datasets for downstream consumption.
Integrate with Salesforce: Collaborate with Senior Salesforce Developers and Enterprise Architects to map staged Snowflake data into standard and custom Salesforce objects.
Active Mentorship & Agile Sprints: Participate in daily stand-ups, backlog grooming, and architectural design reviews alongside senior systems engineers.
Testing & Documentation: Document data dictionaries, entity-relationship diagrams (ERDs), integration flows, and automated validation tests to ensure maintainability.
AI & Automation Exploration: Leverage AI-assisted developer workflows and modern automation tooling to accelerate querying, schema mapping, and documentation generation.
Experience you’ll bring:
Educational Foundation: Pursuing a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Software Engineering, or a related field.
Analytical Mindset: A natural curiosity and tenacity for digging beneath the surface of complex systems to figure out how data flows, where discrepancies lie, and which source represents the ground truth.
Passion for Reusable Systems: An instinct to build tools, scripts, and data models that solve problems systematically rather than with one-off manual patches.
SQL & Relational Foundations: Solid academic or project experience writing structured SQL queries (joins, aggregations, window functions) and understanding relational database principles (foreign keys, indexing, entity relationships).
Scripting & Programming Fundamentals: Working knowledge of at least one programming or scripting language (e.g., Python, Java) and standard version control workflows (Git/GitHub).
Rapid Platform Learner: While prior hands-on experience with Snowflake or Salesforce is a plus, a demonstrable aptitude and enthusiasm to learn both enterprise platforms quickly is paramount.
Clear Technical Communication: Ability to translate complex data structures into plain language when interviewing stakeholders and gathering requirements.
